routines.title: Hamstring & Calf Recovery
routines.subtitle: Ease heavy, sore legs after a hard session.
needs: A pillow for under the ankles
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Stand up slowly — the legs will feel loose. Drink some water and walk about for a minute. Leave heavy lifting until tomorrow.

routines.title: Full Body Express
routines.subtitle: Head to toe in twenty unhurried minutes.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Let them lie still for a minute before sitting up. Water, something warm to wear, and a slow start to whatever is next.

routines.title: Office Chair 10-Minute
routines.subtitle: A proper shoulder rub at a desk, fully dressed.
needs: No oil — everyone stays fully dressed
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Roll the shoulders a few times before standing. Drink some water. Try to move about once an hour for the rest of the day.

routines.title: Hand & Wrist, Seated
routines.subtitle: Six gentle minutes for hands that ache.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Do the second hand even if only one aches — hands like to match. A warm drink afterwards helps stiff joints.

routines.title: Foot Reflexology, Socks Off
routines.subtitle: Ten minutes for feet that have been standing all day.
needs: A firm cushion for your lap
Socks off — everything else stays on
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Get up slowly and put socks back on — feet cool down fast. Drink some water. Do the second foot the same day if you can.

routines.title: Hand Exchange
routines.subtitle: You both give and both receive, at the same time.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Shake both hands out and have some water. If one of you is much stronger, agree a lighter number before the next round.

steps.title: Rest your hands and breathe
steps.body: Lay both palms flat on the back of one thigh. Stay completely still and take three slow breaths together.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth soaking in. Nothing moving yet.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Both of you: breathe out slowly
steps.voiceScript: Lay both palms flat on the back of one thigh and just leave them there. No movement yet. Take three slow breaths together and let the leg get heavy.
steps.commonMistake: Don't dive into deep work on a sore leg. Warm it first.

steps.title: Check the calf before pressing
steps.body: Ask them: any pain, swelling, warmth or redness in one calf, or any blood thinners? If yes to any of it, skip the calves today.
steps.sensationCue: Nothing yet. This is a question, not a stroke.
steps.rhythm: Unhurried. Wait for a clear answer.
steps.voiceScript: Before you press the calf at all, ask one question. Any pain, swelling, warmth or redness in one calf, or are they taking blood thinners? If the answer is yes to any of that, leave the calves alone today, work the thighs only, and get it looked at by a doctor.
steps.commonMistake: Don't assume it is just gym soreness. Ask out loud, every time.
steps.caution: A hot, swollen or tender calf on one side needs a doctor, not massage.

steps.title: Long warming glides up the leg
steps.body: Glide both palms from the ankle up the calf and hamstring, then lightly back down. Float over the back of the knee.
steps.sensationCue: Smooth, warm and unhurried. Nothing sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every five seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: let the leg go heavy
steps.voiceScript: Use both palms and glide slowly from the ankle all the way up the back of the leg. Float lightly over the back of the knee — no pressure at all there. Then slide back down and go again.
steps.commonMistake: Don't stop at the knee. Keep the stroke long and continuous.
steps.caution: Glide over the back of the knee. Never press into it.

steps.title: Forearm down the hamstring
steps.body: Lay your soft forearm across the back of the thigh and lean your weight in. Travel slowly toward the knee and stop well above it.
steps.sensationCue: Broad, deep and dull. A good ache, never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every fifteen seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out as the pressure sinks
steps.voiceScript: Lay your forearm flat across the back of the thigh, keeping the arm soft rather than bony. Lean your body weight in and travel down toward the knee very slowly. Stop a hand's width above the knee and lift off.
steps.commonMistake: Don't push with your arm. Lean in and let your weight do the work.
steps.caution: Stop a hand's width above the knee.

steps.title: Knead the hamstring
steps.body: Take a full handful of hamstring, squeeze, lift it slightly and roll it like dough. Work up and down the thigh, then swap legs.
steps.sensationCue: A satisfying ache that eases as you work.
steps.rhythm: About one squeeze per second
steps.breathCue: Receiver: keep breathing out slowly
steps.voiceScript: Take a full handful of the hamstring — whole hand, not fingertips. Squeeze, lift it slightly away from the bone and roll it between your hands like dough. Work up and down the thigh, then do the other leg.
steps.commonMistake: Don't pinch with fingertips. Use the whole flat of your hand.

steps.title: Squeeze the calf
steps.body: Wrap one hand around the calf, squeeze, then release. Work upward from the ankle and stop a hand's width below the knee.
steps.sensationCue: A firm, hugging squeeze. Dull, never sharp or tingly.
steps.rhythm: Squeeze for two seconds, release for one
steps.breathCue: Receiver: speak up early if it's too much
steps.voiceScript: Wrap your whole hand around the calf and squeeze gently, then let go. Move a little higher each time, working up from the ankle. Stop a hand's width below the knee and never squeeze into the soft crease behind it.
steps.commonMistake: Don't work into the soft crease behind the knee. Stay below it.
steps.caution: Stop if you find a hard, hot or tender lump. Never press behind the knee.

steps.title: Thumb-walk up the calf
steps.body: Set both thumbs low on the calf, either side of the middle. Press, hold two seconds, then walk up a thumb-width and press again.
steps.sensationCue: Small tight spots that soften under steady pressure.
steps.rhythm: One step every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out on each press
steps.voiceScript: Put both thumbs low on the calf, one either side of the middle. Press in, hold for a couple of seconds, then walk them up a thumb-width and press again. Finish well before the back of the knee and start low again.
steps.commonMistake: Don't drag your thumbs. Lift and place them, like footsteps.
steps.caution: Never press into the back of the knee.

steps.title: Work the heel cord
steps.body: Pinch the cord at the back of the ankle between thumb and fingers. Slide slowly up and down it, then cup the heel and circle the foot.
steps.sensationCue: A narrow line of tenderness that eases off.
steps.rhythm: Slow — about three seconds each way
steps.voiceScript: Find the firm cord at the back of the ankle, just above the heel. Pinch it gently between your thumb and fingers and slide up and down a few times. Then cup the heel and circle the whole foot slowly, three times each way.
steps.commonMistake: Don't grip hard here. This cord sits right under the skin.

steps.title: Ease the calf into a stretch
steps.body: Bend their knee to a right angle, cup the heel, and press the ball of the foot gently toward the shin. Hold thirty seconds, then swap legs.
steps.sensationCue: A long pull down the calf. A stretch, never a pinch.
steps.rhythm: Hold still for thirty seconds each side
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out into the stretch
steps.voiceScript: Bend their knee so the lower leg points at the ceiling. Cup the heel in one hand and press gently on the ball of the foot with the other, until they feel a long pull down the calf. Hold about thirty seconds, let it go slowly, then do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Don't bounce it. Steady pressure, then a slow release.
steps.caution: Ease off the moment they feel a pinch or a sharp pull.

steps.title: Long light strokes to finish
steps.body: Stroke both legs from ankle to hip, getting lighter with every pass. Finish with your hands resting still on their calves.
steps.sensationCue: Light and warm. The session closing down.
steps.rhythm: Slower and lighter every pass
steps.breathCue: Both of you: three slow breaths
steps.voiceScript: Sweep both hands from ankle to hip over the whole leg, getting a little lighter with every pass. When it feels finished, rest your hands still on their calves for a few breaths. Then lift away slowly.

steps.title: Rest your hands and settle
steps.body: Rest one palm between their shoulder blades and one on the lower back. Stay still for three slow breaths together.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth spreading. Their shoulders drop.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Both of you: breathe out slowly
steps.voiceScript: Rest one palm between their shoulder blades and the other on their lower back. Don't move at all. Take three slow breaths together and wait for their body to settle.
steps.commonMistake: Don't start rubbing straight away. The pause is the point.

steps.title: Warm the whole back
steps.body: Glide both palms up either side of the spine, out across the shoulders, then lightly down the sides. Repeat without lifting your hands.
steps.sensationCue: Long, smooth and warm. Nothing sharp.
steps.rhythm: One full loop every eight seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: let your back get heavy
steps.voiceScript: Warm oil in your palms first, then glide both hands up either side of the spine. Fan out across the shoulders and slide lightly back down the sides. Keep your hands on them the whole way round.
steps.commonMistake: Don't lift your hands between passes. Keep contact all the way.
steps.caution: Stay off the spine itself. Work the muscle either side of it.

steps.title: Forearm beside the spine
steps.body: Lay your soft forearm alongside the spine and lean in. Travel slowly from the shoulder blade down to the waist, then do the other side.
steps.sensationCue: Broad, deep and dull. A good ache, never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every twenty seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out as it sinks in
steps.voiceScript: Lay your forearm down alongside the spine, keeping it soft rather than bony. Lean your weight in and travel from the shoulder blade slowly down to the waist. Two or three passes each side, then swap.
steps.commonMistake: Don't lead with your elbow point. Use the flat, fleshy part.
steps.caution: Never on the spine itself — stay in the muscle beside it.

steps.title: Knead the shoulders
steps.body: Grip the top of each shoulder between thumb and fingers. Squeeze, lift slightly and roll it, like kneading dough.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, satisfying ache that eases as you work.
steps.rhythm: About one squeeze per second
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out as you squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Grip the top of the shoulder between your thumb and fingers. Squeeze, lift slightly and roll the muscle, like kneading dough. Work out toward the arm and back in toward the neck.
steps.commonMistake: Don't pinch with fingertips. Use the whole flat of your fingers.
steps.caution: Stay off the bony ridge of the collarbone.

steps.title: Ask, then press the glutes
steps.body: Ask first — is it okay to work the glutes over the towel? With a clear yes, lean the heel of your hand in and hold ten seconds a spot.
steps.sensationCue: Deep and broad. It should feel like relief, not force.
steps.rhythm: Ten seconds on, then move a hand's width
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out as the weight arrives
steps.voiceScript: This area stays covered — clothing or a towel over it, always. Ask out loud whether it's okay to work the glutes, and wait for a clear yes. Then lean the heel of your hand in, hold for about ten seconds, and move on a hand's width at a time.
steps.commonMistake: Don't skip the question. Asking is what makes this comfortable.
steps.caution: Keep clothing or a towel in place here. Stop at once if they ask you to.

steps.title: Work the hamstrings
steps.body: Take a full handful of hamstring, squeeze, lift and roll it. Work up and down the thigh, then swap legs.
steps.sensationCue: A satisfying ache that softens as you work.
steps.rhythm: About one squeeze per second
steps.breathCue: Receiver: let the leg go heavy
steps.voiceScript: Take a whole handful of the back of the thigh. Squeeze, lift it slightly and roll it between your hands. Work up and down the thigh, stopping well above the knee, then do the other leg.
steps.commonMistake: Don't grab with fingertips. Whole hand, every time.
steps.caution: Stop a hand's width above the back of the knee.

steps.title: Squeeze the calves
steps.body: Wrap a hand around the calf, squeeze, then release, moving up from the ankle. Stop well below the back of the knee.
steps.sensationCue: A firm, hugging squeeze. Dull, never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Squeeze for two seconds, release for one
steps.voiceScript: Wrap your whole hand round the calf and squeeze, then let go and move a little higher. Work from the ankle up and stop a hand's width below the knee. Then do the same on the other leg.
steps.caution: Never press behind the knee. Skip the calves if either one is swollen, hot or sore.

steps.title: Press and stroke the feet
steps.body: Sandwich one foot between both hands and stroke from toes to heel. Then thumb-walk up the arch in small steps.
steps.sensationCue: Tender spots that ease after a few seconds.
steps.rhythm: One thumb step every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out on the tender spots
steps.voiceScript: Hold the foot between both hands and stroke firmly from the toes back to the heel a few times. Then press your thumb into the heel and walk it forward along the arch in small bites. Forty-five seconds each foot.
steps.commonMistake: Don't tickle. Firm contact from the start stops that.

steps.title: Turn over and glide the arms
steps.body: Ask them to roll onto their back and re-cover them. Glide both palms from wrist to shoulder and lightly back, three times each arm.
steps.sensationCue: Long, smooth and warm down the whole arm.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every eight seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: let the arm go floppy
steps.voiceScript: Hold the towel in place and ask them to roll over onto their back. Cover them again before you carry on. Then glide both palms from the wrist all the way up to the shoulder, and lightly back down, three times on each arm.
steps.commonMistake: Don't rush the turn. Keep them covered the whole way.
steps.caution: Keep out of the armpit. Stop at the shoulder.

steps.title: Squeeze and open the hands
steps.body: Sandwich one hand between yours and squeeze gently. Then set both thumbs in the palm and draw them slowly apart.
steps.sensationCue: The palm opening out. Deep but comfortable.
steps.rhythm: Slow — about five seconds per spread
steps.voiceScript: Take one hand between both of yours and squeeze it gently all over. Then turn it palm up, set both your thumbs in the middle and draw them slowly apart. Finish by sliding down each finger, then do the other hand.
steps.commonMistake: Don't crack or pull the fingers. Slide and squeeze only.

steps.title: Soften the front shoulders
steps.body: Sit at their head and rest a palm on the front of each shoulder. Press gently down toward the bed and hold for twenty seconds.
steps.sensationCue: The chest opening. Shoulders sinking from the ears.
steps.rhythm: Twenty seconds on, ten seconds off
steps.breathCue: Receiver: press down a little more on each out-breath
steps.voiceScript: Sit or kneel at their head. Rest a palm on the front of each shoulder and press gently down toward the bed, so the shoulders settle away from their ears. Hold twenty seconds, ease off, and repeat a few times.
steps.commonMistake: Don't press hard. This is weight, not force.
steps.caution: Press down toward the bed only. Never in toward the throat.

steps.title: Scalp circles, then finish
steps.body: Spread your fingertips over their scalp and move the skin in slow circles. Finish with both hands still, then lift away slowly.
steps.sensationCue: A spreading, sleepy tingle across the whole head.
steps.rhythm: Slow circles, about one per second
steps.breathCue: Both of you: three slow breaths at the end
steps.voiceScript: Spread your fingertips over their scalp like a claw and move the skin itself in slow circles. Cover the whole head, from the hairline to the back. Then rest both hands still, take three breaths together, and lift your hands away slowly.
steps.commonMistake: Don't scratch or drag the hair. Move the skin, not your fingers.

steps.title: Ask first, then rest your hands
steps.body: Check they want a shoulder rub and agree a word that means stop. Then rest both palms flat on their shoulders for three breaths.
steps.sensationCue: Steady weight on the shoulders. Nothing moving yet.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out and let the shoulders drop
steps.voiceScript: Ask whether they'd like a shoulder rub, and agree a word that means stop. Then rest both palms flat on top of their shoulders and stay still for three slow breaths. Everyone stays fully dressed for this one.
steps.commonMistake: Don't start without asking. Ten seconds of asking makes the rest work.

steps.title: Press down along the shoulders
steps.body: Place both palms on top of the shoulders and press straight down for three seconds. Lift, move out an inch, and press again.
steps.sensationCue: Steady, even pressure. Firm but never pinching.
steps.rhythm: Three seconds on, one second off
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out as the weight arrives
steps.voiceScript: Put both palms flat on top of their shoulders, near the neck. Lean your weight straight down for about three seconds, then lift and move an inch further out. Work out to the arms and back in again.
steps.commonMistake: Don't push forward. Press straight down through the chair.

steps.title: Squeeze the top of the shoulders
steps.body: Grip the muscle on top of each shoulder between thumb and fingers, then squeeze, hold a second and release. Work outward and back in.
steps.sensationCue: A firm squeeze that eases as the muscle softens.
steps.rhythm: About one squeeze per second
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out on each squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Grip the ridge of muscle on top of the shoulder between your thumb and fingers, right through their shirt. Squeeze, hold for a second, and release. Work out toward the arm and back in toward the neck, both sides.
steps.commonMistake: Don't pinch with fingertips. Use the whole flat of your fingers.
steps.caution: Stay off the bony ridge of the collarbone.

steps.title: Press either side of the spine
steps.body: Put the heels of your hands either side of the spine, below the neck. Press in and slightly down for three seconds, then step down a hand.
steps.sensationCue: Broad, dull pressure that lands in the muscle.
steps.rhythm: Three seconds on, then move down
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out as you press
steps.voiceScript: Place the heels of both hands either side of the spine, just below the neck. Press in and slightly downward for three seconds, then move a hand's width lower and press again. Go down to the bottom of the shoulder blades and start again at the top.
steps.commonMistake: Don't press while they're breathing in. Time it with the out-breath.
steps.caution: Never press on the spine itself. Stay in the muscle either side.

steps.title: Circle around the shoulder blades
steps.body: Make slow, firm circles with your fingertips around the edge of each shoulder blade. Follow the bony rim, never over it.
steps.sensationCue: Small gritty spots that smooth out as you go.
steps.rhythm: One small circle per second
steps.voiceScript: Find the edge of the shoulder blade with your fingertips — it's the bony rim you can feel through their shirt. Make small firm circles all the way round that rim, working slowly. Then do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Don't circle on the bone. Work the muscle right beside it.

steps.title: Slow circles on the neck
steps.body: Steady their forehead with one hand. With the other, make small circles up the back and sides of the neck with your fingertips.
steps.sensationCue: The neck lengthening. Never sharp, never dizzy.
steps.rhythm: Slow circles, about one per second
steps.breathCue: Receiver: keep breathing normally
steps.voiceScript: Rest one hand lightly on their forehead so the head is supported. With your other hand, make small slow circles up the back and sides of the neck, from the shoulders to the base of the skull. Back and sides only.
steps.commonMistake: Don't let their head hang forward unsupported.
steps.caution: Back and sides of the neck only. Never the front of the throat.

steps.title: Squeeze down the arms
steps.body: Wrap both hands around the upper arm and squeeze for two seconds. Release, move down a hand's width, and repeat to the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: A firm, even hug travelling down the arm.
steps.rhythm: Two seconds on, one second off
steps.voiceScript: Wrap both hands around the top of their arm, over the sleeve, and squeeze for a couple of seconds. Let go, drop a hand's width lower, and squeeze again all the way to the wrist. Then do the other arm.
steps.commonMistake: Don't squeeze the elbow itself. Work above and below it.
steps.caution: Stay on the outside of the arm. Keep out of the armpit.

steps.title: Work the hands
steps.body: Take one hand in both of yours. Press both thumbs into the palm and draw them apart, then squeeze each finger from base to tip.
steps.sensationCue: The palm spreading open. Firm and steady.
steps.rhythm: About five seconds per spread
steps.voiceScript: Come round to the side and take one of their hands in both of yours. Set both thumbs in the middle of the palm and draw them slowly apart, opening the hand out. Then slide down each finger in turn and swap hands.
steps.commonMistake: Don't pull or crack the fingers. Slide and squeeze only.

steps.title: Slow circles over the scalp
steps.body: Spread your fingertips over their head and move the skin in slow circles. Cover the whole scalp, from above the ears to the crown.
steps.sensationCue: A gentle tingle spreading over the head.
steps.rhythm: Slow circles, about one per second
steps.breathCue: Receiver: eyes closed if that helps
steps.voiceScript: Spread your fingers over their head like a claw and move the skin itself in slow circles. Work from above the ears up over the crown and round to the back. Keep it slow — this is the part that switches people off.
steps.commonMistake: Don't scratch or drag the hair. Move the skin, not your fingers.

steps.title: Rest your hands and finish
steps.body: Rest both palms on their shoulders again. Three slow breaths, then lift your hands away slowly.
steps.sensationCue: Stillness. The shoulders sitting lower than before.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Both of you: three slow breaths
steps.voiceScript: Rest both palms back on top of their shoulders and stay still. Three slow breaths, no movement. Then lift your hands away slowly and let them sit for a moment before they stand up.
steps.commonMistake: Don't finish with a slap or a rub. Lift away slowly.

steps.title: Ask first and check for soreness
steps.body: Ask which joints are sore and whether the skin marks easily. Then hold their hand still between both of yours for three breaths.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth passing between your hands. Nothing moving.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Both of you: breathe out slowly
steps.voiceScript: Sit beside them so their forearm rests on the cushion. Ask which joints are sore and whether their skin bruises or marks easily. Then take their hand between both of yours and hold it still for three slow breaths.
steps.commonMistake: Don't guess their pressure. Ask, then ask again once you start.
steps.caution: Thin skin and stiff, swollen joints need much lighter pressure. Start at about a two out of ten.

steps.title: Warm the whole hand
steps.body: Sandwich their hand between your palms and stroke slowly from fingertips to wrist. Repeat, keeping the pressure light and even.
steps.sensationCue: Even warmth spreading through a cold hand.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: let the hand go floppy
steps.voiceScript: Warm your own hands first — rub them together for a few seconds. Then sandwich their hand between your palms and stroke slowly from the fingertips down to the wrist. Light and even, over and over.
steps.commonMistake: Don't start with cold hands. Warm yours first.

steps.title: Stroke the back of the hand
steps.body: Rest their palm down on the cushion. Glide your thumb along each groove between the long bones, from the knuckles toward the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: Narrow lines of easing tightness. Never scraping.
steps.rhythm: One slow line every three seconds
steps.voiceScript: Turn their hand palm down on the cushion. Feel for the grooves between the long bones on the back of the hand, and slide your thumb along each one from the knuckle toward the wrist. Four grooves, a couple of passes each.
steps.commonMistake: Don't press on the knuckle bones themselves. Stay in the grooves.
steps.caution: The skin here is thin. Keep your nails short and your pressure light.

steps.title: Open the palm
steps.body: Turn the hand over and set both thumbs in the middle of the palm. Draw them slowly apart, opening the hand outward.
steps.sensationCue: The palm broadening. A slow, comfortable spread.
steps.rhythm: Five seconds to open, five to release
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out as the palm opens
steps.voiceScript: Turn the hand palm up and support the back of it with your fingers. Place both your thumbs in the middle of the palm and draw them slowly apart, so the hand opens out. Hold for a moment, release, and do it again a little higher and a little lower.
steps.commonMistake: Don't force a stiff hand flat. Open only as far as it goes easily.

steps.title: Circle the thumb mound
steps.body: Find the fleshy pad at the base of their thumb. Make small, slow circles into it with your own thumb for about half a minute.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache in a spot that works hard.
steps.rhythm: One small circle per second
steps.voiceScript: Find the fleshy mound at the base of their thumb — it does most of the work when you grip anything. Press your own thumb into it and make small, slow circles. Pause a few seconds on any spot that feels tight.
steps.commonMistake: Don't rush this spot. It softens slowly.

steps.title: Ease each finger in turn
steps.body: Hold a finger between your thumb and forefinger and slide from base to tip. Add one small circle at each knuckle, then move on.
steps.sensationCue: A small, gentle release in each joint.
steps.rhythm: About eight seconds per finger
steps.voiceScript: Take one finger between your thumb and forefinger and slide gently from the base out to the tip. Add one small circle around each knuckle as you pass it. Work through all five, thumb included.
steps.commonMistake: Don't work only the fingers people mention. Do all five.
steps.caution: Never pull, crack or twist a finger. Swollen knuckles get stroking only.

steps.title: Loosen the wrist
steps.body: Support their forearm on the cushion and cup the hand. Circle the wrist slowly three times each way, only as far as it moves easily.
steps.sensationCue: Easy movement. No clicking, catching or pinching.
steps.rhythm: About four seconds per circle
steps.breathCue: Receiver: let the arm stay heavy
steps.voiceScript: Keep their forearm resting on the cushion and cup their hand in yours. Circle the wrist slowly, three times one way and three the other. Go only as far as it moves easily and stop the moment anything catches.
steps.commonMistake: Don't circle a stiff wrist quickly. Slow and small is better.
steps.caution: Stop if it clicks, catches or hurts. Never force the range.

steps.title: Warm it and finish
steps.body: Sandwich the hand again and stroke from fingertips to wrist, lighter each time. Hold it still, then start again on the other hand.
steps.sensationCue: Light, warm and finished.
steps.rhythm: Slower and lighter every pass
steps.breathCue: Both of you: three slow breaths
steps.voiceScript: Sandwich the hand between your palms one last time and stroke from fingertips to wrist, getting lighter with every pass. Then hold it still for three breaths and set it down gently. Now do the same on the other hand.

steps.title: Settle the foot and check in
steps.body: Rest their heel on the cushion on your lap. Ask about diabetes, numbness or sore spots, and look the foot over before you start.
steps.sensationCue: Just weight and warmth. Nothing moving yet.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Both of you: breathe out slowly
steps.voiceScript: Put the cushion on your lap and rest their heel on it, socks off, everything else stays on. Ask whether they have diabetes or any numbness in the feet, and have a proper look at the skin. Then hold the foot still for a few breaths.
steps.commonMistake: Don't skip the look. Cuts, blisters and sore spots are easy to miss.
steps.caution: With diabetes or numb feet, use light pressure only and stop if the skin is broken.

steps.title: Warm the whole foot
steps.body: Sandwich the foot between both palms and stroke firmly from toes to ankle, over and over. Keep both hands in contact throughout.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth and blood coming into a cold foot.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: let the foot go heavy
steps.voiceScript: Sandwich the foot between both of your palms, one on the sole and one on top. Stroke firmly from the toes back toward the ankle, over and over. Firm contact from the very first stroke — that's what stops it tickling.
steps.commonMistake: Don't start light. A light touch on feet just tickles.

steps.title: Circle the ankle slowly
steps.body: Hold the heel still in one hand and cup the toes with the other. Circle the foot three times each way, only as far as it goes easily.
steps.sensationCue: Easy movement. No clicking or pinching.
steps.rhythm: About four seconds per circle
steps.voiceScript: Hold the heel firmly in one hand so it doesn't move. With the other hand, cup the toes and circle the whole foot slowly, three times each way. Small circles are fine — never force it further than it wants to go.
steps.commonMistake: Don't circle from the toes alone. Hold the heel still.

steps.title: Thumb-walk up the arch
steps.body: Press your thumb into the heel and walk it forward along the arch in small bites, like a caterpillar. Do three passes.
steps.sensationCue: Tender spots that ease with a few seconds of pressure.
steps.rhythm: One step every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out on the tender spots
steps.voiceScript: Support the top of the foot with your fingers and press your thumb into the heel. Bend and straighten the thumb to walk it forward along the arch in tiny bites, like a caterpillar. Three passes, and pause on anything that feels tight.
steps.commonMistake: Don't slide. Press, ease off, move a little, press again.

steps.title: Open the sole
steps.body: Place both thumbs in the centre of the sole and draw them slowly apart, opening the foot outward. Repeat a little higher and lower.
steps.sensationCue: The sole broadening. A slow spreading stretch.
steps.rhythm: Five seconds to open, five to release
steps.breathCue: Receiver: breathe out as it opens
steps.voiceScript: Wrap your fingers around the top of the foot and set both thumbs in the middle of the sole. Draw them slowly apart so the foot opens outward, hold a moment, then release. Do it again nearer the toes and nearer the heel.

steps.title: Press the ball of the foot
steps.body: Work your thumb across the padded ball of the foot below the toes. Press and hold three seconds on any spot that feels tight.
steps.sensationCue: A firm, dull press. Never burning or sharp.
steps.rhythm: Three seconds on, then move along
steps.voiceScript: Move up to the padded ball of the foot, just below the toes. Press your thumb in and hold for about three seconds, then move along a little and press again. Work right across from the big toe side to the little toe side.
steps.commonMistake: Don't dig with the tip of your thumb. Use the flat pad.

steps.title: Work the heel
steps.body: Make firm, slow circles into the fleshy pad of the heel with your knuckles. Keep the foot supported on the cushion throughout.
steps.sensationCue: Deep, dull and satisfying. Never sharp or burning.
steps.rhythm: One slow circle per second
steps.breathCue: Receiver: say the word if it's too much
steps.voiceScript: Make a loose fist and put your knuckles into the fleshy pad of the heel. Make firm, slow circles, letting the cushion take the weight underneath. This is the toughest skin on the body, so it takes more pressure than the rest.
steps.commonMistake: Don't work fast. Slow circles go deeper than quick ones.
steps.caution: Ease right off if they have diabetes or any numbness in the feet.

steps.title: Trace between the long bones
steps.body: Turn to the top of the foot. Slide your thumb along each groove between the long bones, from the toes back toward the ankle.
steps.sensationCue: Narrow lines of tenderness releasing. Never scraping.
steps.rhythm: One slow line every three seconds
steps.voiceScript: Turn your attention to the top of the foot. Feel for the grooves between the long bones and slide your thumb along each one, from the toes back toward the ankle. Light pressure — the skin here is thin.
steps.commonMistake: Don't press on the bones. Stay in the grooves between them.
steps.caution: The skin on top of the foot is thin. Keep it light.

steps.title: Ease each toe
steps.body: Take each toe in turn, squeeze gently from base to tip, then circle it once each way. Move on without pulling or cracking.
steps.sensationCue: A tiny release in each joint.
steps.rhythm: About twelve seconds per toe
steps.voiceScript: Take each toe between your thumb and forefinger and squeeze gently from the base out to the tip. Then circle it once each way and move to the next one. Work through all five, and don't be tempted to pull them.
steps.commonMistake: Don't skip the little toe. It gets the most squashed.
steps.caution: Never yank or crack a toe. Squeeze and circle only.

steps.title: Long strokes, then swap feet
steps.body: Stroke the whole foot from toes to ankle, getting lighter each pass. Rest both hands still, then start again on the other foot.
steps.sensationCue: Light, warm and finished.
steps.rhythm: Slower and lighter every pass
steps.breathCue: Both of you: three slow breaths
steps.voiceScript: Sandwich the foot between both palms again and stroke from toes to ankle, getting lighter every time. Rest your hands still for three breaths, then set the foot down. Do the whole thing again on the other side — feet like to match.
steps.commonMistake: Don't stop at one foot. The other will feel left out.

steps.title: Sit facing and hold still
steps.body: Sit facing each other with knees close. Both of you take one of the other's hands between your palms and hold still for three breaths.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth building between four still hands.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Both of you: breathe out slowly
steps.voiceScript: Sit facing each other with your knees close, so nobody has to reach. Both of you take one of the other person's hands between your palms. Hold completely still and take three slow breaths together.
steps.commonMistake: Don't rush past this. The stillness sets the pace for both of you.

steps.title: Warm each other's hand
steps.body: Both of you stroke slowly from their fingertips down to the wrist and back. Match each other's speed and keep the pressure light.
steps.sensationCue: Even warmth. Two hands moving at one pace.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Both of you: breathe slowly and evenly
steps.voiceScript: Both of you now: sandwich their hand between your palms and stroke slowly from the fingertips down to the wrist, then back again. Try to match each other's speed. Light and even is all this needs.
steps.commonMistake: Don't race each other. Slow down to whoever is slower.

steps.title: Stroke the back of the hand
steps.body: Both of you turn their hand palm down. Glide your thumb along each groove between the long bones, from the knuckles toward the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: Narrow lines of easing tightness. Never scraping.
steps.rhythm: One slow line every three seconds
steps.voiceScript: Both of you turn the hand you're holding palm down. Feel for the grooves between the long bones on the back of the hand, and slide your thumb along each one toward the wrist. Four grooves each, a couple of passes.
steps.commonMistake: Don't press on the knuckle bones. Stay in the grooves.
steps.caution: The skin here is thin. Keep your nails short and your pressure light.

steps.title: Open the palm together
steps.body: Both of you turn the hand over and set both thumbs in the middle of the palm. Draw them slowly apart, opening the hand outward.
steps.sensationCue: The palm spreading open. Slow and comfortable.
steps.rhythm: Five seconds to open, five to release
steps.breathCue: Both of you: breathe out as the palm opens
steps.voiceScript: Both of you turn the hand palm up and support the back of it with your fingers. Set both thumbs in the middle of the palm and draw them slowly apart so the hand opens out. Hold, release, then do it again a little higher.
steps.commonMistake: Don't force it flat. Open only as far as it goes easily.

steps.title: Circle the thumb mound
steps.body: Both of you find the fleshy pad at the base of their thumb. Make small, slow circles into it and pause on anything that feels tight.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache in a hard-working spot.
steps.rhythm: One small circle per second
steps.voiceScript: Both of you find the fleshy mound at the base of their thumb. Press your own thumb into it and make small, slow circles. If you find a tight spot, stay on it for a few seconds and let it soften.
steps.commonMistake: Don't grind. Steady circles do more than hard pressure.

steps.title: Work each finger in turn
steps.body: Both of you take a finger between thumb and forefinger and slide from base to tip. Add one small circle at each knuckle, then move on.
steps.sensationCue: A small, gentle release in each joint.
steps.rhythm: About eight seconds per finger
steps.voiceScript: Both of you take one finger between your thumb and forefinger and slide gently from base to tip. Circle each knuckle once on the way past. Work through all five, thumb included, and tell each other if anything is sore.
steps.commonMistake: Don't work only the fingers they mention. Do all five.
steps.caution: Never pull, crack or twist a finger.

steps.title: Swap hands and repeat
steps.body: Both of you let go and take the other hand. Run the same moves again — warm it, stroke the back, open the palm, then the fingers.
steps.sensationCue: The second hand catching up with the first.
steps.rhythm: About fifteen seconds per move
steps.breathCue: Both of you: keep breathing slowly
steps.voiceScript: Both of you let go and take the other hand instead. Run through the same four moves — warm it, stroke the back, open the palm, then the fingers. About fifteen seconds each, and keep matching each other's pace.
steps.commonMistake: Don't shortchange the second hand. Give it the same care.

steps.title: Hold still and finish
steps.body: Both of you hold the other's hand between your palms again. Three slow breaths together, then let go at the same time.
steps.sensationCue: Still, warm and even. Both hands the same.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Both of you: breathe out slowly
steps.voiceScript: Both of you take the hand between your palms one last time and hold it completely still. Three slow breaths together, no movement. Then let go at the same time and shake your own hands out.
